Stan Kroenke is an American billionaire businessman.
Stan Kroenke was born on July 29, 1947.
Stan Kroenke is the owner of Kroenke Sports & Entertainment.

Kroenke Sports & Entertainment owns Arsenal F.C., Arsenal W.F.C., Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche, Colorado Rapids, Colorado Mammoth, Los Angeles Gladiators, and Los Angeles Guerrillas.
Kroenke Sports & Entertainment also owns Screaming Eagle Winery and Vineyards and Waggoner Ranch.
Stan Kroenke's wife is Ann Walton Kroenke (m. 1974).
Ann Walton Kroenke is part of the Walton family.
Ann Walton Kroenke is the daughter of James "Bud" Walton, co-founder of Walmart.
Stan Kroenke was estimated to be worth US$10.7 billion by Forbes in 2022.

Kroenke's teams have won five championships under his ownership: two Super Bowls with the Rams, two Stanley Cups with the Avalanche, one NBA Championship with the Nuggets, an MLS Cup with the Rapids, and two National Lacrosse League Championships with the Mammoth.
Stan Kroenke grew up in Mora, Missouri.
Mora is an unincorporated community with a population of approximately 24 people.
Kroenke's father owned Mora Lumber Company.
Kroenke's first job was sweeping the floor at his father's lumber yard by age 10.
At Cole Camp High School, Kroenke played baseball, basketball, and ran track.
Stan Kroenke founded the Kroenke Group in 1983.
The Kroenke Group is a real estate development firm that has built shopping centers and apartment buildings.
Kroenke is also the chairman of THF Realty, an independent real estate development company specializing in suburban development.
THF Realty was founded by Kroenke in St. Louis, Missouri, in 1991.
In 2016, THF's portfolio was valued at over $2 billion, including more than 100 projects totaling 20 million square feet primarily in retail shopping centers.
Kroenke acquired Screaming Eagle Winery and Vineyards in partnership with Charles Banks in 2006.
In April 2009, Banks stated he was no longer personally involved with Screaming Eagle.
Kroenke is a major owner of working ranches, owning a total of 848,631 acres.
The Land Report magazine ranked Kroenke as the United States' ninth-largest landowner in 2015.
In February 2016, Kroenke acquired the famous Waggoner Ranch in Texas.
Kroenke is involved in launching a British outdoor sports television channel that includes hunting programmes featuring killing of elephants and lions.
Stan Kroenke became full owner of both the Denver Nuggets and Colorado Avalanche in 2000.
The purchase was from Charlie Lyons's Ascent Entertainment Group.
In 2002, Kroenke partnered with Pat Bowlen and John Elway to become part-owner of the Colorado Crush.
Kroenke purchased the Colorado Mammoth and Colorado Rapids from Phil Anschutz in 2004.
On April 13, 1995, Kroenke helped move the Los Angeles Rams to St. Louis by purchasing a 30% share of the team.
In 2010, Kroenke exercised his right of first refusal to purchase the remaining interest in the Rams from the Frontiere estate.
On August 25, 2010, Kroenke became full owner of the Rams by unanimous consent of the NFL.
Kroenke agreed to turn over control of the Denver Nuggets and Colorado Avalanche to his son, Josh, by the end of 2010.
Kroenke gave up his majority stake in both teams in December 2014.
Stan Kroenke said he would attempt to keep the Rams in St. Louis in April 2010.
The Rams' lease at Edward Jones Dome had an escape clause that allowed them to break their original lease and assume a year-to-year agreement.
In February 2013, the Rams and City of St. Louis went to arbitration over a clause in the Rams' lease.
The arbitrators agreed with the Rams, giving them the ability to break their original lease.
Stan Kroenke met with Missouri Governor Jay Nixon at Rams Park on November 30, 2015, to discuss stadium issues.
On January 5, 2015, the Kroenke Group announced plans for a new NFL stadium in Inglewood, California.
The city of St. Louis offered to build an open-air stadium dubbed National Car Rental Field in the north riverfront area of downtown.
Kroenke stated that St. Louis was no longer a viable market for the NFL and was best served by only two teams.
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell stated that the St. Louis funding did not meet the criteria set by the NFL.
St. Louis officials said Kroenke was misrepresenting the city at owners' meetings.
The Oakland Raiders and San Diego Chargers had been proposing a stadium in Carson, California, as competition to Kroenke's Inglewood proposal.
On January 4, 2016, all three teams applied for relocation to Los Angeles for the 2016 NFL season.
On January 12, 2016, the NFL approved the Rams' application to move from St. Louis back to Los Angeles with a 30–2 vote.
The Chargers announced their intention to play in Carson initially and then move into Kroenke's Inglewood Stadium pending completion.
The Raiders subsequently announced they would move to Las Vegas, Nevada.

On April 12, 2017, the City of St. Louis, St. Louis County, and the Regional Convention and Sports Complex Authority filed a lawsuit against the NFL and all 32 NFL clubs as defendants (including Stan Kroenke).
The lawsuit sought damages and restitution of profits.
On July 12, 2017, the Los Angeles Rams filed motions to dismiss the case for failure to state a claim, lack of personal jurisdiction, and appeal to have the case determined through arbitration.
The motions were decided upon by Judge Christopher McGraugh.
On April 20, 2020, the Supreme Court denied Kroenke and the NFL's appeal of the lawsuit.
On November 24, 2021, a $790 million settlement was agreed to end the lawsuit.
Kroenke is the owner of Arsenal Holdings plc, which owns Arsenal F.C. and Arsenal W.F.C.
Granada Ventures sold its 9.9% stake in Arsenal Holdings plc to Kroenke's KSE UK inc. in April 2007.
By June 2008, the board had prepared to let Kroenke take over.
On September 19, 2008, it was officially announced that Kroenke had joined the board of directors.
Kroenke controlled voting rights over 18,594 shares, representing 29.9% of the issued shares.
Nearing the maximum 29.99% threshold, Kroenke agreed to make an offer for the rest of the club at £11,750 per share, valuing the club at £731M.
In August 2018, Kroenke made a £600M offer accepted by Alisher Usmanov, bringing his ownership beyond 90% and forcing compulsory purchase of remaining shares.
In April 2021, Arsenal were announced as founding members of the European Super League.
Arsenal backed out within two days after strong backlash.
Kroenke's family released a statement saying they would not sell the club.
Stan Kroenke developed the Los Angeles Gladiators in the Overwatch League in late 2017.
The inaugural season began on December 6, 2017.
In 2019, KSE founded the Los Angeles Guerrillas of the Call of Duty League.
Both teams are based out of Hollywood Park next to where Kroenke's Rams play.
Kroenke experienced a unique feat in 2022 with three of his teams winning championships: the Rams, Mammoth, and Avalanche.
In 2023, Kroenke's Denver Nuggets won the NBA Championship.
This gave him four different sports titles in a 16-month span.
